title: free-disk-space commands
description: The subcommands of the free-disk-space binary, as main.rs parses and dispatches them. Errors print `error: ...` to stderr and exit with status 1 (util::die); a second Ctrl-C exits with 130. Nothing checks who the caller is: every command runs with the invoking user's permissions, and the file system decides what it may read or change. The same commands can be run as `zazzle free-disk-space ...`: the zazzle invoker in macos/c/zazzle/ replaces itself with this binary, found beside it, and passes the arguments on unchanged.

entities.name: Start a scan
entities.description: Starts a new compression scan of a directory tree and runs it until it finishes or is stopped.
entities.transport: free-disk-space new [--root DIR] [--min-size SIZE] [--min-age-days N] [--min-savings-pct N] [--cross-devices] [--exclude PATH]... [--force] [--state FILE]
entities.authorization: None checked; it reads what the invoking user can read, and directories it cannot read are counted as errors.
entities.result: A new state file; progress on one line, then `Scan complete` with the candidate count and estimated saving, or `Scan paused` after Ctrl-C.
failures: --root is not a directory: exits with an error.
An unfinished scan exists and --force is not given: exits with an error naming the pending directory count.
--min-size is not a size: exits with an error.
The state file cannot be opened: exits with an error.

entities.name: Resume a scan
entities.description: Continues an interrupted scan with the settings it was started with.
entities.result: The same output as new, starting from the pending directories; `Scan already complete` if nothing is pending.
failures: No state file: exits with an error pointing at new.
The state file holds no scan configuration: exits with an error.

entities.name: Show scan status
entities.description: Shows the scan's root, progress, candidates by status, recorded file names and current free space.
entities.result: Root; complete or in progress with queued directories; directories, files, bytes, errors and elapsed time; per status the file count, estimated and verified savings; file names recorded and replaced by clones; free space on the data volume.
failures: No state file: exits with an error pointing at new.

entities.name: List candidates
entities.description: Lists candidates of one status, largest estimated saving first.
entities.result: One line per candidate: size, estimated saving, path and its note; `(none with status ...)` when empty.
failures: No state file: exits with an error pointing at new.

entities.name: Compress candidates
entities.description: Compresses pending candidates in place with APFS compression, each through a verified temp copy.
entities.transport: free-disk-space compress [--sample N] [--max-files N] [--limit SIZE] [--min-age-days N] [--min-gain SIZE] [--reserve SIZE] [--dry-run] [--yes] [--state FILE]
entities.authorization: None checked beyond the file system: a file is skipped unless its directory is writable. On a terminal it asks `Compress these files in place? [y/N]` unless --yes; when stdout is not a terminal it does not ask.
entities.result: The plan (file count and estimated saving); a progress line with the position in the plan, the files compressed and not compressed, the saving so far and the elapsed time; a FAILED line with a note for each failed file; then the initial and final free space, counts, how many files were skipped for each reason (with a pointer to list --status skipped), the verified allocated-space saving and the overall free-space change, which it says can differ.
failures: Not macOS and FDS_FORCE unset: exits with an error.
/usr/bin/ditto missing: exits with an error; nothing changed.
On macOS, not --dry-run, ditto --hfsCompression writes an uncompressed probe copy (the message names macOS 26/27): exits with an error before asking; nothing changed.
No state file: exits with an error pointing at new.
--limit is not a size: exits with an error.
No pending candidates: prints so and stops.
The scan has not finished: warns and works from the candidates found so far.
Three failures in a row: prints that it is aborting for safety and stops.

entities.name: Replace duplicates with clones
entities.description: Finds byte-identical same-named, same-sized files the scan recorded and, with --apply, replaces all but one with copy-on-write clones of the kept copy.
entities.authorization: None checked beyond the file system; without --include-system it leaves out files owned by root or by another user and files under system paths (is_system_file).
entities.result: A dry run unless --apply: the number of name groups, then each clone made (or, dry, up to 50 that would be, followed by a line saying it is still hashing and the totals come at the end), the counts, and the allocated size of the replaced files as an upper bound on the saving; with --apply also the free-space change on the volume.
failures: --apply off macOS without FDS_FORCE: exits with an error.
No state file: exits with an error pointing at new.
No file names recorded in the state: exits with an error asking for a new scan.
--apply and lsof gives no snapshot of open files: exits with an error; nothing changed.
The scan has not finished: warns and works from the file names found so far.
A clone fails verification: prints FAILED with the reason and keeps the original; three in a row abort the run.

entities.name: Clean regenerable files
entities.description: Deletes caches, Xcode derived data, Downloads, Trash contents, old dev build artifacts, Homebrew's cache and Docker's images and build cache, as chosen.
entities.transport: free-disk-space clean TARGET... [--apply] [--dev-root DIR] [--docker-stop-timeout SECONDS], TARGET one of all, caches, downloads, trash, dev, docker, brew, xcode (all = caches, downloads, trash, dev, docker)
entities.authorization: None checked; deletions the user may not make are listed as protected and skipped. A dry run unless --apply.
entities.result: Per folder and per dev artifact what was (or would be) removed, its size and the running total; with --apply after an interrupted run, a line saying how many steps are already done and `done before the interruption` for each folder or target it skips; after each target the elapsed time and free space; initial and final free space; the sum of sizes seen and, with --apply, the actual free-space change; Docker's state; protected, failed and uncertain entries, 30 at most each.
failures: No target given: clap refuses the command line.
A file or directory cannot be removed: listed as protected; the run goes on.
Finder's empty trash fails, a docker prune or stop fails, or Docker does not quit: listed under failures.
A dev artifact cannot be proved regenerable: listed as uncertain and left alone.

entities.name: Run the daemon
entities.description: Runs in the foreground, checking free space every cadence of awake time and cleaning when it is below the threshold; this is what the login item executes.
entities.transport: free-disk-space daemon run [--threshold SIZE|PCT%] [--cadence 90s|15m|2h] [--targets TARGET...] [--dev-root DIR]; started by launchd at login once installed
entities.authorization: None checked; it deletes with the invoking user's permissions, as clean --apply does.
entities.result: Timestamped log lines: started, then per check ok, below threshold (followed by clean's output) or skipped; stopped on Ctrl-C.
failures: The threshold is not a positive size or a percentage between 0 and 100, or the cadence is not a positive number of s, m or h: exits with an error.
The display is asleep or the volume cannot be read: the check is logged as skipped and the next one waits a full cadence.

entities.name: Install the daemon
entities.description: Writes the launchd plist for this binary's path and settings, and starts it as a login item.
entities.transport: free-disk-space daemon install [--threshold SIZE|PCT%] [--cadence 90s|15m|2h] [--targets TARGET...] [--dev-root DIR]
entities.authorization: None checked; launchd accepts it in the invoking user's gui domain.
entities.result: ~/Library/LaunchAgents/local.free-disk-space.plist written, any earlier instance booted out and the new one bootstrapped; prints the plist path, the settings, the log path and how to remove it.
failures: Invalid threshold or cadence: exits with an error before writing anything.
The binary cannot find its own path: exits with an error.
The LaunchAgents or Logs directory cannot be created, or the plist cannot be written: exits with an error.
launchctl bootstrap fails: removes the plist and exits with launchctl's output.

entities.name: Uninstall the daemon
entities.description: Stops the login item and removes its plist.
entities.result: `Removed <plist path>`, or `Not installed.`; the log file is kept.
failures: The plist exists but cannot be removed: exits with an error.

entities.name: Show daemon status
entities.description: Shows whether the login item is installed and running, and where it logs.
entities.result: Login item installed or not (with the plist path), running yes or no (launchctl print), and the log path.

relatedViews.relationship: The capabilities these commands belong to.
The use cases that call these commands.
new and resume drive the scan's lifecycle.
compress moves candidates out of pending.
